name: schedule-readback
title: Schedule Readback
description: Cron input that reads the expression back in plain English, lists the next runs in your time zone beside the scheduler's, and catches every-minute stars, day-of-month OR day-of-week, the 31st skipping months and 30 February, with one-tap fixes.

meta.stops: Cron job fires at the wrong time
mistakes: cron day of week or month
meta.summary: Reads a cron expression back in plain English with the next runs in your zone and the server's, catching classic cron traps.
catches: A * in the minute field that runs every minute
Day-of-month and day-of-week both set, which runs on either (OR)
Day 31 (or 29–30) skipping shorter months, and impossible dates like 30 Feb
Scheduler zone differing from yours, with runs shown in both
limits: 5-field Vixie/POSIX cron only; Quartz seconds/years, Jenkins H and cloud-specific syntaxes are not supported
Next runs are computed in the browser; DST handling depends on the zones you pass
a11y: Visible <label>; aria-invalid with read-back via aria-describedby
Parse errors use role=alert; read-back and warnings render in polite live regions
Each fix button has an aria-label with the corrected expression; focus returns to the input after a fix

rules.note: Confirmed: when both day-of-month and day-of-week are restricted, the job runs when either matches. Other schedulers (systemd, Quartz, cloud cron) differ.
